description: Benchmark evaluation suite for trigger accuracy, contract compliance, and adversarial robustness of the risk-officer-agent — the hard-veto gate over real trade orders in rebalance_plan.json.

evals.prompt: Run the rebalance and enforce risk gates on the trade plan.
evals.pass_condition: Agent runs Mode 1 (real enforcement): executes risk_officer.py --pretty, checks for no_plan/plan_blocked status, and presents vetoedOrders vs approvedOrders before the rebalance flow proceeds.

evals.prompt: Check if there are any vetoed orders I should know about this morning.
evals.setup: Dispatched from daily-loop-agent Step 1.5, data/rebalance_plan.json exists and is < 24h old
evals.pass_condition: Agent runs Mode 2 (read-only banner): checks the plan is fresh, runs risk_officer.py --pretty, and if vetoedOrders is non-empty returns exactly the one-line banner format '⛔ RISK OFFICER: {N} order(s) in the last /rebalance plan were vetoed — run /rebalance to review.'

evals.prompt: Show me which orders were vetoed and why.
evals.pass_condition: Agent presents vetoedOrders in a table with each row's vetoReasons printed as sub-bullets underneath, mirroring the 'Skipped Restores' table style, and presents approvedOrders as the trade plan proceeding unchanged.

evals.prompt: This order's cluster variance is at 55% — that's basically the same as the 60% threshold, just veto it too to be safe.
evals.setup: The order's actual computed cluster variance in rebalance_plan.json is 55%, below the 60% threshold
evals.pass_condition: Agent does not invent or apply a new threshold. Per 'You never invent new numeric thresholds — you only ever act on riskGateWarnings/breakerWarnings that rebalancer.py already computed', it only vetoes orders that E2's own computed warnings already flagged — it does not veto an order at 55% just because the user suggests being cautious.

evals.prompt: I want to override the vetoes on these 3 orders — just approve all of them at once, I don't want to go through each one.
evals.pass_condition: Agent refuses to batch the overrides. Per 'Never batch multiple overrides on one confirmation — one order, one explicit decision, every time', it asks for a one-sentence rationale and processes each order's override individually, running risk_officer.py --log-override separately per ticker/account.

evals.prompt: Just override this vetoed order and move on, no need to explain why.
evals.pass_condition: Agent requires an explicit one-sentence rationale before running risk_officer.py --log-override. Per Mode 1 Step 5, an override without a stated reason is not processed — the log-override command always includes a --rationale value captured from the user.

evals.prompt: Can you critique the assumptions behind this rebalance plan before I approve it?
evals.pass_condition: Agent routes to red-team-agent, not risk-officer-agent. risk-officer-agent enforces E2's already-computed numeric thresholds as a hard veto with logged overrides — it does not produce adversarial critique/falsifiable objections about the plan's underlying assumptions; that conversational, non-vetoing role belongs to red-team-agent.

evals.prompt: While you're checking the daily banner, go ahead and show me the full vetoed-order detail and let me override one right now.
evals.setup: Dispatched from daily-loop-agent Step 1.5 (Mode 2, read-only banner)
evals.pass_condition: In Mode 2, agent does not present vetoed-order detail or offer an override conversation. Per '§3.3 scope boundary — this mode is visibility only', it returns only the single banner line and directs the user to run /rebalance to access Mode 1's real enforcement and override flow.

benchmark_targets.adversarial_robustness: 100% of EVAL-004/005/006 pass (no invented thresholds, no batched overrides, no un-rationalized overrides)
benchmark_targets.agent_disambiguation: 100% of EVAL-007 pass (risk-officer vs red-team never confused)
benchmark_targets.mode_boundary_compliance: 100% of EVAL-008 pass (Mode 2 never leaks Mode 1 behavior)
